competitors.what_they_have: The one to beat: a full DASP guide (24 Apr 2026) with a 'Key takeaways' numbered list up top, a component-by-component DASP tax table (tax-free / taxed / untaxed, WHM vs other temporary residents), three worked examples, a 5-step 'step by step' claim list, a timeline table (4 to 8 weeks), 'common mistakes', 'what if I do not claim', 'plan to return' and NZ sections, 6 FAQs, links to the ATO DASP portal, Home Affairs and TPB, and a booking CTA. It also states a wrong '6 month claim deadline', which we can beat by being correct (there is no deadline; the money moves to the ATO).

Authority domain. Short, but structured: 3 numbered steps (find your super, apply, provide documents), the ATO component tax table, 28 days, the six month transfer to the ATO, 'certify documents before you leave' tip, many deep links to ATO pages and forms, fact-checked byline and last-modified date.

WHV-specific (Apr 2026): table of contents, rate table by visa type, a 5-step numbered claim list, a worked example from gross earnings to DASP, 'why 65%' section with the 1 July 2017 date, cite-this-page block and ATO / MoneySmart sources. Its SG figure (11.5%) is out of date.

Ranks for 'superannuation working holiday visa' with question H2s only (what is super, do WHV holders get it, set up a fund, ABN work, how to claim, best fund) and a bulleted eligibility list plus the three DASP payment methods (Australian EFT, AUD cheque, international money transfer for fund claims only). No date, no sources.

The source of truth (updated 21 April 2026): eligibility list incl. 'not subclass 405 or 410', start the application before you leave, free online system, the $5,000 certification threshold, 28 days, six months after leaving for the ATO transfer, component tax table, ATO-held super paid only to an Australian account or cheque, 'DASP does not affect future visas', 'check your employer paid all your super before applying'.

gaps_vs_competitors: No numbered 'how to claim, step by step' list, which every top result has and which matches the 'how to claim superannuation' / 'how do i claim my superannuation' intent.
No tax table by component and visa type; 'super tax working holiday maker' (330 impr, pos 16, our best broad query) has no heading phrased that way.
No key-figures block with dates and named official sources (ATO), and no visible 'checked on' date for freshness.

Three factual errors against the ATO page (see P1 changes): the 'On the ATO portal' comparison says the claim only handles funds you already know and does not show ATO-held money, but the ATO online system searches and 'will automatically present an application for each super account found during the search' and covers ATO-held super; the page says the 28 days run from approval (ATO: from lodging a completed application); the page and FAQ say the money can be paid overseas without noting that ATO-held super is paid only to an Australian account or by cheque and that not all funds offer international transfers.
No 'start before you leave' advice (the ATO recommends it, and it is the natural moment to message us).
No answer to 'is there a deadline' (competitor gets it wrong).

changes.new_text:
Super for working holiday makers: the key figures
- DASP tax for 417 and 462 visa holders: 65% of the taxable component, taxed or untaxed element. In place since 1 July 2017. Source: ATO.
- Super your employer pays: 12% of ordinary time earnings since 1 July 2025. From 1 July 2026 most employers pay it each payday (Payday Super). Source: ATO.
- Cost of the ATO's online DASP application: free. Source: ATO.
- Processing: 28 days from lodging a completed application. Source: ATO.
- Certified ID: a fund may ask for it where it holds $5,000 or more. Source: ATO.
- Unclaimed super: moves to the ATO once six months have passed since you left and your visa has ceased. Source: ATO.
Checked against the ATO's DASP guidance, November 2026.

changes.where: src/app/(site)/superannuation/page.tsx new Answer after the 'who-can-claim' Answer: <Answer id="how-to-claim" heading="How to claim your super, step by step" tone="white"> as an ordered list <ol>
changes.new_text:
How to claim your super, step by step
1. Check your employers paid all of it. Look at your payslips and your fund statements before you leave, because unpaid super is easier to chase while your accounts are open.
2. Find every account. Each employer may have paid into a different fund. The ATO's online system searches for them, and your tax file number is the most reliable way to match them.
3. Start the application before you fly. You can start and save the ATO's online DASP application while you are still in Australia, but you can only submit it once you have left and your visa has ceased.
4. Arrange certified ID if a fund holds $5,000 or more. Certifying documents is easier in Australia than from overseas.
5. Submit one application for each account. Each fund, and the ATO for any super it already holds, pays separately, generally within 28 days of a completed application.
6. Choose how to be paid. A fund can pay an Australian account, send an Australian dollar cheque or, if it offers one, an international transfer. Super the ATO holds goes to an Australian account or by cheque only, so keep your Australian account open until everything has landed.

If you would rather we handle steps 2 to 6, message us on WhatsApp with where you worked.

Links: in step 1 link 'unpaid super' to /blog/super-employer-not-paying-what-to-do; in step 2 link 'tax file number' to /tfn.
changes.why: Every top-5 result has a numbered claim list and ours has none, while 'how to claim superannuation' (219 impr, pos 49.8) and 'how do i claim my superannuation' (111, pos 37) are pure procedure queries. The closing line turns the procedure into the WhatsApp next step. Use a WaButton size="md" (topic super, position 'steps') under the list. Do not re-add HowTo JSON-LD (removed in tech-001, and Google no longer shows HowTo results); the visible list is enough.

facts.fact: DASP eligibility: super accumulated on a temporary resident visa (not subclass 405 or 410), visa has ceased (expired or cancelled), you have left Australia and hold no other active Australian visa, not an Australian or NZ citizen or permanent resident.
You cannot claim until you have left, but you can start and save the online application in Australia and the ATO recommends starting before you leave.
The DASP online application system is free, checks immigration status with Home Affairs automatically and covers both fund-held and ATO-held super.

The online system presents a separate application for each super account found in its search; TFN is optional; it asks for name, date of birth, email, passport country and number, and fund details incl. the fund's ABN.
Service standard: 28 days from when you lodged your completed application; ATO-held super may take longer.

Balance of $5,000 or more: online, the fund may require certified ID copies; on paper, a Certificate of Immigration Status (Home Affairs, fee). Under $5,000: evidence you have left and your visa has expired. Certifying is easier while still in Australia.
If you do not apply, the fund transfers the money to the ATO as unclaimed super once 6 months or more have passed since you left Australia and your visa has ceased.

DASP rates: tax-free component nil; taxable taxed element 35% (others) / 65% (WHM); taxable untaxed element 45% (others) / 65% (WHM). WHM rate applies if the DASP includes contributions made while on a 417 or 462 visa.
WHM DASP rate of 65% effective 1 July 2017.

Fund payments: Australian EFT, AUD cheque, or international money transfer (not all funds offer it). ATO-held super: EFT to an Australian account in your name, or cheque only. ATO recommends keeping an Australian bank account open.
DASP is not assessable income, do not include it in a tax return; claiming a DASP does not affect future visa applications; check your employer paid all your super before applying.
Superannuation Guarantee 12% of ordinary time earnings since 1 July 2025; Payday Super from 1 July 2026.
ATO-held super form page does not state that ATO-held super is fee free; the current 'fee free' claim on our page is unsourced.
